ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the length to which the current segment grows: hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the buffer or its length and the limit on unchanged, and hop 2 only copies the characters into a new array of the length it gets from hop 3. The gold's javadoc promises the length to which a buffer GROWS when it needs room for more characters; for the 262144-character segment of the trigger (MAX_SEGMENT_LEN) the variant gold returns 262144, no growth, so the expansion stops and testExpand fails. Once the gold has returned that length, a longer segment can appear only if a caller replaces or overrides the gold's result. The convention that expanding the current segment always makes it longer, also at and beyond MAX_SEGMENT_LEN (the cap applies only to new segments, in TextBuffer.expand and finishCurrentSegment), is pinned outside the gold: the sibling overload TextBuffer.expandCurrentSegment(int) grows the current segment to the requested size with no cap at MAX_SEGMENT_LEN; the production caller UTF8StreamJsonParser.addName writes cbuf[cix++] right after 'if (cix >= cbuf.length) cbuf = _textBuffer.expandCurrentSegment();', relying on a longer segment; the facade's javadoc says the expansion is 'to accommodate for more contiguous content'; and TestTextBuffer::testSimple passes through the chain (200 -> 300, a non-null larger buffer).
